steps.name: Blend the sky in the window

lines.text: Inside the outlined area. Its top is at the top edge, and its left side is at the left edge; it's about 1 1/4 in wide and 1 3/4 in tall.
Paints, top to bottom: Pale sky blue, then Warm white.
Mix enough Warm white for this step and steps 5, 15 and 21; cover it between them.
Brush: 3/4 inch wash brush. Load: Creamy paint. An even coat.
Start with the darkest color and stroke side to side. Without rinsing, pick up the next lighter color and paint below it. Then stroke back up over the join several times.
It should leave smooth bands of color, with a soft join where two wet colors meet.
Watch out: Blending after the paint has started to drag. Acrylic sets in minutes, and scrubbing setting paint lifts it and leaves streaks. Fix: stop as soon as it drags.
Let it dry, then blend a new thin layer on top.

steps.meant: The left quarter of the canvas, from the top down to the sill line, is a smooth pale blue sky. The rest of the canvas is bare white.

steps.name: Dab the dark leaves

lines.text: Let the sky through the window dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is about 1/2 in from the top edge, and its left side is about 1 in from the left edge; it's about 1/4 in wide and 1 1/4 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the white window frame and the frame's shadows will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the sky through the window, painted already: there, only soften this paint into its edge and leave it showing.
Paint: Leaf green.
Brush: old stiff brush. Load: A light load. No water on the brush: a wet one makes blobs.
Tap with the tip of the brush. The more you tap one spot, the more solid it gets.
It should leave dots or dappled patches that get more solid the more you tap.
Watch out: Blobs instead of dots. The brush is too wet or holds too much paint. Fix: wipe most of the paint off on a paper towel and tap again.

steps.meant: Loose dark green leaf clumps fill the window opening, pale sky showing between them. No bright leaves yet; the rest of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Dab the sunlit leaves

lines.text: Let the leaves outside the window and the sky through the window dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area. Its top is about 1/2 in from the top edge, and its left side is about 1 in from the left edge; it's about 1/4 in wide and 1 1/4 in tall.
The outline also runs under where the white window frame and the frame's shadows will go: paint straight through there.
The outline also reaches onto the sky through the window, painted already: there, only soften this paint into its edge and leave it showing.
Paint: Sunny leaf green.
Brush: old stiff brush. Load: A light load. No water on the brush: a wet one makes blobs.
Tap with the tip of the brush. The more you tap one spot, the more solid it gets.
It should leave dots or dappled patches that get more solid the more you tap.
Leave what step 2 painted showing around these marks, as in the Result picture.
Watch out: Blobs instead of dots. The brush is too wet or holds too much paint. Fix: wipe most of the paint off on a paper towel and tap again.
Step back, squint, or take a photo to see it whole, and compare the big shapes with the picture.

steps.meant: The leaves outside are finished: dark green clumps with bright yellow-green tops against pale sky. The rest of the canvas is bare.
